title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
abstract:
Deforestation-reducing development pathways may cut emissions, but it is unclear how workers can adapt given skill and geographic mobility constraints. Modelling job transitions in Brazil reveals that greener pathways benefit workers in high-skill occupations but increase low-skill unemployment, mitigated by mobility policies. 
 Deforestation is a major source of global greenhouse gas emissions, and continued forest loss risks pushing the Amazon from a carbon sink to a carbon source. While recent work shows that productivity-led structural transformation towards less land-intensive sectors can reduce deforestation, the labour market implications of such pathways remain poorly understood. Here we address this gap by developing a spatially and occupationally explicit agent-based labour market model informed by empirically observed job-transition networks to simulate the ability of workers to respond to labour demand shocks. Our analysis reveals significant skill and geographic mobility frictions that constrain workers’ ability to adapt to structural change. Applying the model to productivity-driven development scenarios, we find that pathways delivering the largest deforestation and emission reductions disproportionately benefit high-skill workers while increasing unemployment among agricultural and other low-skill workers. Mobility-enhancing labour market policies can mitigate these effects, highlighting the importance of understanding labour market dynamics for equitable and feasible deforestation-reducing development pathways. title: Nickel isotopes in Apollo and Chang’e soils reveal widespread micrometeorite-driven processing of the lunar regolith
abstract:
Micrometeorite-driven processing causes widespread heavy Ni isotope enrichment across the lunar surface, although local signatures can be modified by regolith maturity and the addition of Ni-rich materials, according to Ni isotope analysis of lunar soils. 
 Micrometeorite bombardment is a fundamental surface process on the Moon and other airless bodies, driving elemental evaporation, isotopic fractionation, and material mixing in surface regoliths. Here, we report high-precision stable Ni isotope data for lunar soils returned by the Apollo (11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17) and Chang’e (5 and 6) missions, covering geographically and geologically diverse lunar terrains. The analyzed soils show δ60/58Ni values of 0.345‰ to 1.280‰ (relative to NIST SRM 986), generally heavier than lunar basalts and the inferred bulk silicate Moon, indicating widespread heavy Ni isotope enrichment during surface processing. Together with published Chang’e-5 drill-core data, these results demonstrate that micrometeorite-driven Ni isotope fractionation is widespread across the lunar surface. Local variability, however, reflects additional controls. The relatively low δ60/58Ni values of the immature Apollo 12 soils are consistent with limited cumulative micrometeorite processing, whereas the mature Apollo 16 soils have high Ni concentrations and Ni/Co ratios, indicating additional compositional overprinting by Ni-rich material. Stable Ni isotopes, particularly when combined with regolith maturity and Ni/Co ratios, therefore provide a sensitive tracer of micrometeorite-driven lunar surface processing and its local overprinting. title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
abstract:
At the watershed scale, remote sensing maps land use and estimates pollution loads; at the lake scale, it provides water quality data for models; at field and interface scales, it identifies nutrient-loss hotspots, based on a review of remote sensing to approaches aquatic nutrients. 
 Leveraging its capability for large-scale, repeated monitoring, remote sensing has increasingly supported nitrogen and phosphorus estimation in surface waters. However, the evolution of this field from proxy-based nutrient retrieval to integration with process-based models remains insufficiently synthesized. Here we review remote sensing approaches for estimating aquatic nutrients, with emphasis on their roles in supporting process-based modeling, and compare their methodologies, applications, and limitations. At the watershed scale, remote sensing supports land use mapping and pollution load estimation, identifying nutrient sources and constraining transport simulations. At the lake scale, it provides continuous observations and water quality products that inform hydrodynamic and water quality models. At the field and interface scales, remote sensing helps identify hotspots of nutrient loss by capturing the heterogeneity of management practices. Despite these advances, nutrient estimation remains constrained by proxy relationships and spatial scale. Future research should integrate remote sensing with hydrodynamic and biogeochemical models to constrain nutrient fluxes and improve mechanistic understanding of aquatic nutrient cycling. title: Global ice loss drives source-independent amplification of sea-level rise at Pacific and Indian Ocean Small Island Developing States
abstract:
Many Pacific and Indian Ocean small island developing states are located within persistent sea-level-rise hotspots, according to glacier mass flux and sea level projections. 
 We quantify the spatial pattern (“fingerprint”) of sea-level rise caused by mass loss from the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets and from glaciers worldwide through 2100. Using ensembles of ice-sheet and glacier mass-balance projections and gravitational, rotational, and deformational sea-level modeling, we calculate normalized sea-level fingerprints and their impacts on Small Island Developing States. We show that Small Island Developing States in the Pacific and Indian Oceans are located within persistent sea-level-rise hotspots where the ice-melt contribution to local sea-level rise systematically exceeds the global mean by up to ~ 24%. This amplification emerges regardless of whether meltwater originates from Greenland, Antarctica, or the global glacier system. We identify a source-independent and geographically systematic amplification of sea-level rise affecting some of the world’s most climate-vulnerable nations. Many Pacific and Indian Ocean small island developing states are located within persistent sea-level-rise hotspots, according to glacier mass flux and sea level projections.

title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
abstract:
Australian rivers emit 48.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis. 
 Streams and rivers are major contributors to global emissions of carbon dioxide and methane, yet seasonal hydrological variability in discharge and river surface area is often not fully represented in large-scale emission estimates. Here, we integrate riverine and dry riverbed carbon dioxide and methane data with geospatial data of the Australian drainage network to predict emissions at a monthly time-step. We show that flowing Australian rivers emit a total of 48.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis. Spatiotemporal emission patterns closely follow variations in river surface area, with contrasting seasonal pulses from tropical regions in the wet season and temperate regions in winter. These results highlight the importance of hydrological dynamics, particularly the seasonal expansion and contraction of river networks, in governing riverine emissions across Australia. title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives
abstract:
The identification of previously unrecognised eruptions and improved correlations between ice cave deposits and other volcanic archives refine the eruptive history of Mount Melbourne, according to geochemical analyses and statistical clustering of tephra from three Antarctic ice caves with existing volcanic records. 
 Volcanic deposits preserved within Antarctic fumarolic ice caves provide rare access to sub-ice eruptive records hidden beneath the ice cap. Here we present the first integrated textural, petrological, and geochemical characterisation of 21 tephra samples from three summit ice caves at Mount Melbourne (Northern Victoria Land, Antarctica). Major and trace-element glass compositions, combined with published datasets, were analysed using multivariate statistical workflows. Dimensionality reduction and clustering identified a distinct compositional group with no known equivalent in the existing Mount Melbourne record, suggesting that at least one previously unrecognised Holocene eruption occurred within the investigated Fumarolic Ice Caves. Correspondence between Fumarolic Ice Cave deposits and volcanic signatures in marine sediment, englacial sequences, and other proximal-distal records refined Mount Melbourne’s eruptive history and strengthened tephra correlations across archives. More broadly, sub-ice tephra archives can reveal hidden eruptive histories relevant to volcanic hazard assessment in polar regions. title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
abstract:
Mineral weathering-derived calcium promotes soil organic carbon storage in US Mollisols, and agriculture has increased calcium inputs four- to fivefold, altering the geochemical conditions that sustain carbon in these soils, based on continental-scale datasets and geochemical modelling. 
 Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. We find that calcium released by mineral weathering is associated with soil organic carbon storage and that this effect is stronger in Mollisols than in non-Mollisols. Our model also shows that agriculture has increased calcium inputs to cultivated USA Mollisols 4-5 fold, indicating that humans have fundamentally changed the geochemical conditions that sustain organic carbon in these soils. By implication, moderating the quantity of and timing of calcium release may help to preserve and restore carbon in the world’s most intensively farmed landscapes. Mineral weathering-derived calcium promotes soil organic carbon storage in US Mollisols, and agriculture has increased calcium inputs four- to fivefold, altering the geochemical conditions that sustain carbon in these soils, based on continental-scale datasets and geochemical modelling.

title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
abstract:
The typhoon Hagibis (2019) flood damage was highly influenced by typhoon track variations and levee height, with the highest losses concentrated around Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya under different storm scenarios, according to a methodological framework for assessing typhoon-induced flooding and impact analysis. 
 Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. To systematically evaluate how typhoon-track position and levee height influence flood damage, we conduct longitudinal typhoon-track perturbation experiments and levee-height variation scenario analyses. Here we show that the flood damage is highly sensitive to small typhoon-track shifts, with a 0.2° longitudinal shift causing an average damage difference of 83.3 billion JPY. A 1.0° eastward shift causes the highest damage in Kanto and across Japan, mainly around Tokyo, while 1.6° and 0.4° westward shifts produce the greatest damage in Kinki and Chubu, mainly around Osaka and Nagoya, respectively. The levee-height sensitivity experiments show an average flood-damage reduction of approximately 9.1 billion JPY for each 10% increase in levee height. The typhoon Hagibis (2019) flood damage was highly influenced by typhoon track variations and levee height, with the highest losses concentrated around Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya under different storm scenarios, according to a methodological framework for assessing typhoon-induced flooding and impact analysis.

title: Ocean thermal inertia sustains a tropical Pacific mean state shift under net zero
abstract:
The tropical Pacific shifts towards El Niño-like conditions under ongoing warming and does not recover for centuries after emissions cease, according to climate model simulations spanning centennial to millennial timescales. 
 The tropical Pacific plays a pivotal role in global climate, and changes in its mean state and in the El Niño Southern Oscillation can substantially alter regional hydroclimates with major economic and societal impacts. Yet, its response to different emission pathways remains poorly constrained. Here we assess changes in the tropical Pacific mean state and variability under high emission and net zero scenarios, using climate model simulations spanning centennial to millennial timescales. Under transient warming, the tropical Pacific shifts towards an El Niño-like mean state. Following emission cessation, continued warming of the Southern Ocean and deep ocean sustains this mean state for centuries, driving persistent El Niño-like rainfall anomalies and more frequent extreme El Niño events even as atmospheric carbon dioxide declines. Changes in ENSO amplitude, by contrast, are non-monotonic and more model dependent. Key aspects of tropical Pacific change are therefore effectively irreversible on multi-centennial timescales, and net zero emissions slow further change without restoring pre-industrial conditions. title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe2/WS2 moiré superlattices
abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe2/WS2bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression ofOsFID1in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions inArabidopsishas uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found thatBT2andGSL8transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. TheBT2transcript represses transcription of its targetsCEP2andMRF4by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereasGSL8acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh2(R-3,5-diPheTPCP)4features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogenp-orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metald-orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting fromp-type WSe2multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WOx,n-type WS2, and semimetallic WTe2. This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WOx/WSe2local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia
abstract: The ciliary transition zone (TZ) regulates ciliary proteome composition, yet its molecular architecture, protein content, and contribution to motile ciliopathies remain poorly defined. We applied in situ cryo–electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to human multiciliated epithelial cells. This approach resolved TZ-specific doublet microtubules at subnanometer resolution and identified nine constituent proteins. We found that epithelial cell transforming 2 like (ECT2L) and double zinc ribbon and ankyrin repeat-containing protein 1 (DZANK1) form the major linker complexes between adjacent TZ doublet microtubules. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia.ECT2LandDZANK1deficiency disrupted TZ architecture, caused microtubular abnormalities and abnormal bulbous ciliary tips, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These findings establish a direct genetic link between TZ defects and human motile ciliopathy and illustrate how in situ structural biology can uncover mechanisms of human disease.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception inLotus japonicusandMedicago truncatula. Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: Glycan recognition by a plant damage-sensing immune receptor
abstract: Pathogens target and degrade the extracellular matrix surrounding plant cells. A central question is how cell wall–derived damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are recognized and integrated to trigger immune responses. We address this question by determining the structure of the extracellular multidomain of the impaired in glycan perception 1 (IGP1) receptor in both apo form and bound to the cellulose-derived DAMP cellotriose. Structural analyses reveal that constitutive interactions of leucine-rich repeat (LRR)–malectin domains preconfigure IGP1 for ligand recognition and that the receptor features a highly specific sugar-binding pocket in the LRR domain capable of distinguishing fine variations in glycan structures. By directly sensing cello-oligomers, IGP1 operates as a cell wall surveillance receptor that links pathogen-induced wall degradation to immune alerting, equipping plants to mount rapid and robust defense responses.
